_comment: Ablation: does the encoder do better reading the row as feature tokens (one token per column, FT-Transformer style) or as plain serialized text? Run with: python main.py --config config/text_vs_feature_tokens.json. Architecture, optimizer and splits are identical across the three experiments, so the only difference is how a row reaches the encoder.

experiments.name: feature_tokens
experiments._comment: Control. Sequence is [CLS] + 10 product_name subwords + 2 numeric tokens + 5 categorical tokens = 18 positions.

experiments.name: all_text_matched_columns
experiments._comment: The same eight columns the control uses, serialized as 'name: value | name: value' and read only by the text tokenizer. No numeric or categorical tokens at all, so a win or loss here is about representation, not about which columns the model saw. Longest train row is 60 subwords.

experiments.name: all_text_every_column
experiments._comment: Every column drop_columns leaves, minus the label and query_id, serialized the same way: adds filter_price_min/max, net_weight_oz, ingredients and country_of_origin, which the control never sees. Compare against all_text_matched_columns to separate 'more columns' from 'text instead of feature tokens'. Longest train row is 111 subwords.
